companyDescription: DNA-medicines biotech · INO-3107 under FDA accelerated-approval review for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP) · PDUFA Oct 30, 2026 · cash runway extends past the catalyst
priceNote: Self-fetched today (no live-prices.json cache yet). Near the 52-week low ($1.03), down sharply from the 52-week high ($2.98), heading into the Oct 30, 2026 PDUFA decision for INO-3107.
summary: Inovio's INO-3107 is under FDA accelerated-approval review for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP), a rare disease affecting an estimated 14,000-27,000 US patients with no approved therapy beyond surgical debulking. The FDA completed its mid-cycle review with no new significant issues raised, and a late-cycle review is set for Q3 — both real de-risking signals ahead of the Oct 30, 2026 PDUFA date. The 12-month consensus target of $5.83 implies +445% from here — this is genuinely broad, not a single-analyst outlier. Critically, the company beat Q1 EPS estimates and, after an April 2026 equity raise, has cash runway into Q1 2027 — meaning it can fund operations past the PDUFA date without an emergency raise. That's a real survival advantage most nano-cap binary biotechs don't have.

catalysts.name: INO-3107 PDUFA Decision
catalysts.description: FDA accelerated-approval decision for INO-3107 in recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP). Mid-cycle review completed with no new significant issues; late-cycle review set for Q3 2026 ahead of the final decision.

risks: This is a real binary FDA decision — a Complete Response Letter would remove the entire near-term thesis, and RRP's small patient population means there's little room for a partial/label-restricted approval to still satisfy the market

INO-3107 is a second entrant into this indication — differentiation on efficacy/tolerability/simplicity is the company's own framing, and the market's willingness to pay a premium for that differentiation is untested

Q1 2026 net loss was $19.7M — even with runway into Q1 2027, the company will likely need further capital (the April 2026 raise being one example) before or shortly after the PDUFA date, which is real dilution risk
Nano-cap ($88M) with a 52-week range spanning $1.03-$2.98 — extreme volatility and thin liquidity are real execution risks
The Oct 30 date is still over 3 months out — a long stretch for sentiment to drift on secondhand biotech-sector news before the actual event

estimateDates.est: No new issues expected given the clean mid-cycle review

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed holds at 3.50–3.75%, but new Chair Warsh's hawkish tone has 9 of 18 officials projecting a further 2026 hike, with the next FOMC decision Jul 28–29, 2026.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core inflation remains above target and the 10-year yield sits near 4.48% — a headwind for nano-cap biotechs that periodically need to raise capital, though Inovio's runway into Q1 2027 buys some insulation.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: The PDUFA decision itself is entirely macro-independent — an FDA accelerated-approval ruling doesn't respond to interest rates.
macroRisk.summary: LOW — this is one of the more macro-independent names on the board since the near-term catalyst is a pure regulatory decision, though the broader financing environment still matters for any capital raise around the PDUFA date.
